comparison: Perfect agreement. Both evaluations find the comparative tool engineering studies (C51-C55, C100-C104) well-supported. Reviewers explicitly praised the 'extensive tool engineering studies' and OpenEval noted the measurements are internally consistent with appropriate controls.

Divergence in evaluation. OpenEval finds biosensor validation data (C56-C58) fully supported with appropriate statistical presentation. Peer reviewers rated UNCERTAIN, questioning whether the iSH-Akt biosensor demonstration was necessary for validating these systems.

Agreement with nuance. Both find the membrane tag optimization (C59, C6) supported. OpenEval emphasizes quantified improvement, while peer reviewers accept the approach but suggest potential for further refinement regarding lipid raft targeting.

Strong agreement. Both find GEF specificity validation (C60-C61) supported by biosensor data. OpenEval notes appropriate controls, peer reviewers describe evidence as 'convincing' and affirm specific GTPase activation.

Strong agreement. Both evaluations support the permeability assay findings (C105). OpenEval notes adequate sample sizes and appropriate controls. Peer reviewers explicitly praised the 'clever' use of fluorescent-labeled dextran polymers.

Strong agreement on ECIS resistance measurements (C62-C66). OpenEval emphasizes temporal dynamics and rapid reversibility. Peer reviewers found the 'immediate and repeatable responses' impressive and praised system resiliency. Peer R6 covers broader claim set including C67-C72, C110.

Agreement on differential OptoITSN/OptoTIAM responses (C67-C69). OpenEval documents the partial decrease during extended activation. Peer reviewers grouped these with broader ECIS findings (R6) and found the overall barrier integrity changes 'fascinating and impressive.'

Agreement on OptoP63 biphasic response (C70-C72). OpenEval notes the initial decrease followed by recovery suggests adaptation mechanisms. Peer reviewers included these findings in their broader endorsement of ECIS experiments (R6).

Agreement on morphological observations (C73-C76). OpenEval notes correlation with resistance measurements but limited quantification of overlap. Peer reviewers directly affirmed the connection between observed morphology (lamellipodia, cellular overlaps) and barrier function.

Divergence in certainty. OpenEval rates linearity index findings (C77-C79) as UNCERTAIN, noting these changes don't explain resistance increases. Peer reviewers rated SUPPORTED as part of thorough characterization, though acknowledged incomplete elucidation of mechanism.

Strong agreement on VE-cadherin independence (C80-C83, C111). Both find this critical finding well-supported. OpenEval calls it 'compelling' evidence challenging VE-cadherin-centric view. Peer reviewers strongly endorsed the 'orthogonality' demonstration. Peer R9 also addresses broader mechanistic claims (C8, C10, C112).

Agreement on morphological characterization (C84-C85). OpenEval emphasizes objective quantification via form factor analysis. Peer reviewers accepted these as part of comprehensive validation showing expected GTPase-specific effects.

Agreement on temporal dynamics of cell area changes (C86-C89). OpenEval notes recovery during continued activation parallels resistance recovery. Peer reviewers accepted these morphological changes as aligned with expectations for specific GTPase activation.

Agreement but with acknowledged limitations. OpenEval supports correlation between cell size and resistance (C90) but notes correlation doesn't prove causation. Peer reviewers rated UNCERTAIN, finding results 'compelling' but noting incomplete elucidation of mechanism.

Agreement with limitations. OpenEval supports temporal relationship between overlap increase and resistance (C92) but notes limited quantification. Peer reviewers rated UNCERTAIN, acknowledging the work but noting the mechanistic connection was not fully resolved.

Perfect agreement on spatial control capabilities (C96-C99). OpenEval emphasizes adequate sample sizes and lack of fatigue. Peer reviewers praised the 'precise spatio-temporal control' and called it 'a significant advance.'

Agreement on S1P comparison (C110). OpenEval notes this provides important biological context. Peer reviewers included this in their broader endorsement of ECIS experiments, noting the comparison to physiological stimuli.

OpenEval evaluated technical characterization of LED system (C106-C109) as supported with thorough documentation important for reproducibility. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these specific technical specifications.

Agreement on uncertainty. Both rate cell-cell overlap mechanism (C112-C113) as UNCERTAIN. OpenEval notes evidence is suggestive but mechanism not definitively proven due to technical limitations. Peer reviewers found it 'compelling' but noted incomplete elucidation requiring further investigation.

OpenEval evaluated background literature claims about endothelial biology and Rho GTPase function (C1-C3, C11-C43) as appropriately cited established knowledge. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these contextual claims.

Divergence in evaluation. OpenEval finds background on tool selection (C4, C44-C50) well-supported by literature. Peer reviewers rated UNCERTAIN for C4 specifically, requesting expanded rationale and citations for why p63, ITSN1, and TIAM1 were selected over alternatives.

Strong agreement on overall tool capabilities (C5, C7-C10). OpenEval finds high-level summary statements supported by collective evidence, noting VE-cadherin independence strongly supported. Peer reviewers strongly endorsed tools as 'valuable advance' with 'precise spatio-temporal control.'

Peer reviewers provided comprehensive evaluation of all ECIS findings (C62-C72, C110) in single result, praising immediate/repeatable responses and system resiliency. OpenEval separated these into multiple results (R6, R7, R8, R17) with more granular analysis of each GEF's specific effects.

Peer reviewers grouped VE-cadherin independence findings (C80-C83, C111) with broader mechanistic claims (C8, C10, C112) in single strongly supportive evaluation. OpenEval separated VE-cadherin findings (R11, SUPPORTED) from mechanistic interpretation (R19, UNCERTAIN), showing more cautious assessment of mechanism.
